4 - take walking breaks if needed. There's a very famous marathon prep system that focuses on run / walk balance. Nothing wrong with it, and it's much healthier for newer runners.

5 - focus on your goals. It sounds like you'd like to run consistently. If it truly is something you want to become part of your routine, start slow and steady..... focus on staying healthy. I've lost the last year in trying to rehab because i didn't follow my own advice (took too long of a break after a couple marathons, then jumped back in too fast). Nothing is more frustrating than a nagging, slow-healing injury, which is often the case with minimally vascularized connective tissues.

6 - keep at it!

7 - running outside will change your world. Treadmills really limit your body's motion; running outside can get you to a much more natural gate, and and much more healthy one.

8 - try running barefoot from time to time. Find a local football field or soccer field, and do a few laps on the grass barefoot. Your body will naturally find the most efficient stride, as opposed to the one subsidized by the cushion of shoes.

9 - personal preference here, but audio books on a run are amazing. I've gone through classics such as Homer's Odyssey or Crime and Punishment, history like Undaunted Courage (Lewis and Clark), podcasts, and more. Getting out and getting exercise while relieving stress and learning something ... doesn't get much better than that.

Good luck, and feel free to ask any questions!
